- scripts/ci_budget_watch.py: `main()` body, the try/except around `_gh(...)` + `job_timeouts(...)` (the warning on the exception path) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When PyYAML is missing, `job_timeouts()` raises `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'`. The catch-all `except Exception` then emits `::warning::ci_budget_watch: could not read this run's jobs (...); job durations not checked.` The message claims a jobs-read failure, but the jobs were in fact read successfully; the failure was a YAML import inside `job_timeouts()`.
  WHY: The diagnostic is misleading. Operators triaging a CI warning will look for a GitHub API / token / permission issue when the real cause is a missing PyYAML. The exception detail in parentheses includes the missing module name, so the underlying truth is recoverable, but the lead clause pushes the operator down the wrong path.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
